name: Hercules
introduction: is the hero of the twelve labors, kneeling upside down in the sky with one foot on the head of Draco. It is the fifth-largest constellation. Its central shape, a quadrilateral called the Keystone, is easy to find between Vega and Arcturus on northern summer evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: The Sun is moving roughly toward Hercules. This direction, called the solar apex, lies near the border with Lyra; it is where the Sun and its planets are traveling relative to the nearby stars.

On one side of the Keystone lies M13, the Great Globular Cluster in Hercules, a ball of several hundred thousand stars about 22,000 light-years away. In 1974, the Arecibo radio telescope beamed a message toward it, a greeting that will take about 22,000 years to arrive.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Rasalgethi](hip:84345), the hero’s head, is a red giant with its own companions, a variable star swollen to hundreds of times the Sun’s width. [Kornephoros](hip:80816) is the brightest star.

[Zeta Herculis](hip:81693) and [Mu Herculis](hip:86974) are nearby Sun-like stars, 35 and 27 light-years away, both multiple systems. [Sarin](hip:84379), [Pi Herculis](hip:84380) and [Eta Herculis](hip:81833) frame the Keystone.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Besides M13, Hercules contains a second fine globular cluster, M92, among the oldest in the galaxy. Far beyond it, the Hercules Cluster of galaxies lies about 500 million light-years away.
